transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood PM), Ahmed El-Sayed (Polaris), Lena Korhonen (Polaris), Marco Rivera (Polaris), Sofia Tran (Polaris security)

Auto-generated summary (brief, may be noisy):
Redwood and Polaris kicked off a joint pilot to package Redwood runtimes for Polaris' edge marketplaces - discuss packaging AMI/VM, reference architecture for k8s + on-prem edge, security integrations (SOC2, KMS), and pilot success metrics (latency, qps, cost per token). Next steps to exchange artifacts and schedule the pilot week.

Topics: marketplace packaging, edge reference architecture, pilot scope and SLOs, security/compliance, billing/metering integration, co-marketing

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: ok hi everyone thanks for carving out time. this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with me is Daniel Ruiz our SE and Priya Patel who owns the platform integrations.
[00:16] Ahmed El-Sayed: hey Maya, hi team. really appreciate it, we'll try to be focused. we have a couple of folks from product and security on this one.
[00:23] Lena Korhonen: hey, lena here. thanks.
[00:26] Marco Rivera: Marco here. quick note, we're trying to get a marketplace-ready package that can run on our edge nodes as well as in customer on-prem clusters.
[00:34] Daniel Ruiz: perfect, that's exactly the bit we wanted to align on. goal for today is to lock pilot scope, handoffs, and artifacts needed for the listing and the ref-arch.
[00:43] Sofia Tran: hi, I'm Sofia, security ops. we'll be validating the KMS and data-in-transit controls, also SOC2 artifacts.
[00:52] Maya Chen: great. quick agenda: packaging (image/ami/ova/helm), ref-arch for k8s + edge (resource sizing, autoscaling, fallback), security/compliance, metering and entitlements for marketplace billing, timelines.
[01:07] Ahmed El-Sayed: sounds good. Marco can give 2-min on our target edge profile?
[01:12] Marco Rivera: yes, short version: a lot of our partners run a mixed set — some have small 4-8 vCPU edge appliances with an attached T4-class GPU, others are mid-tier with A10/A100 sized instances. we also have fully air-gapped on-prem customers where they need an offline bundle.
[01:32] Daniel Ruiz: okay so we need to support a couple of runtime artifacts: lightweight quantized models for T4-like GPUs and a high-performance H100/A100 image for bigger sites. packaging options we recommend: 1) pre-baked AMI/VM image for AWS marketplace, 2) OCI container + helm chart for k8s installs, 3) exportable air-gapped bundle with signed binaries and offline license file.
[01:53] Lena Korhonen: when you say quantized, are you talking int8? and is that automatically supported by Redwood runtime?
[01:58] Daniel Ruiz: yes, int8 and some 4-bit paths — runtime supports quantized kernels but performance varies per model. we'll include suggested model variants in the artifact. be aware of accuracy tradeoffs; we'll document recommended prompts and evals.
[02:14] Marco Rivera: also want to capture networking constraints — some edge sites only allow outbound to a proxy on 443, no arbitrary egress.
[02:22] Priya Patel: noted - we'll add an egress-mode that uses a reverse-proxy or a broker for telemetry and token metering. that will be part of the helm values.
[02:30] Sofia Tran: for security, main ask: KMS integration for keys at rest, and ability to route logs to customer SIEM. do you have SOC2 type 2 report?
[02:39] Maya Chen: yes we have SOC2 type 2 — we'll share the attestation link. for KMS we support bringing-your-own key (BYOK) integrations, and HSM options for private deployments. note: in transcript sometimes product names come out funky, we call it Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private but sometimes the q&a shows 'Redwood Dedikate' in the notes.
[02:58] Ahmed El-Sayed: haha okay noted. for marketplace listing we also need entitlements to map usage to our billing. how do we get per-tenant metering?
[03:07] Daniel Ruiz: two options: marketplace metering hooks (we push metering events with token counts) or Polaris handles a service-side ingestion with our usage webhooks. both can be supported. the AMI will have a small agent that batches usage events and signs them.
[03:22] Marco Rivera: any throttles for latency? our customers expect sub-200ms for short prompts, but for long generation 1.5s is okay.
[03:31] Daniel Ruiz: depends on model variant. for small quantized models on T4 you'll usually see 80–200ms for short contexts; larger models on A100/H100 will be higher. we recommended setting SLOs per site type in pilot.
[03:45] Lena Korhonen: how do you handle KV cache or prefix caching at the edge?
[03:49] Daniel Ruiz: the runtime exposes a local KV cache, and we can persist checkpoints to local NVMe. for shared state across nodes, there's an optional sync via the broker, but for edge we usually recommend local-only caching to reduce egress.
[04:05] Priya Patel: also want to call out model fallback behavior — we can configure policy to fall back to hosted variants in Redwood's cloud if latency spikes or if the edge pool is out of capacity. Polaris, is that something you want enabled?
[04:18] Ahmed El-Sayed: yes, but for some regulated customers we cannot allow external calls. so fallback must be opt-in per customer.
[04:27] Maya Chen: totally agree, fallback will be per-entitlement toggle. we'll document it in the runbook.
[04:33] Marco Rivera: on the packaging side, are there signing requirements for images? we require signed artifacts for air-gapped installs.
[04:40] Daniel Ruiz: yes, we'll provide signed tarballs and attestations, and the HVAC... i mean the hash signatures. shipping GPG and SHA256 checksums, plus an optional transparency log we can publish.
[04:56] Sofia Tran: about SSO we need SAML and OIDC support for tenant admin portal.
[05:02] Priya Patel: SSO is supported; we have SAML metadata and OIDC Oauth flows. we'll provide an example OIDC client config and SAML metadata file for the helm chart values.
[05:12] Ahmed El-Sayed: great. now pilot logistics — what do you need from us to start the pilot?
[05:19] Daniel Ruiz: minimally: list of pilot sites (site profile: cpu/gpu type, network constraints), a test dataset and eval prompts, and contact for the ops team. we'll run a smoke deploy, perf runs, and capture token-level latency and cost metrics.
[05:33] Marco Rivera: we can provide two sites: one T4-like appliance and one A100 cloud colocated instance. target pilot window one week — prefer 10/21 to 10/28.
[05:44] Maya Chen: ok we'll aim for 10/21 for smoke and initial perf. Daniel, can you produce a sizing guide and bootstrap scripts?
[05:50] Daniel Ruiz: yes — runbook, terraform snippets for cloud targets, and helm values for k8s. will include minimum NVMe and memory per model variant.
[06:00] Lena Korhonen: are you planning to publish an Azure marketplace image as well? some of our customers are azure-first.
[06:07] Priya Patel: we can provide ARM images/VMs for Azure and images for GCP as part of the listing artifacts — that adds packaging work but doable.
[06:15] Ahmed El-Sayed: on commercial mapping — Polaris wants to embed entitlements so customers can buy the marketplace listing and billing flows into them, do you have standard licensing metering?
[06:25] Maya Chen: yes we have entitlements and API keys mapping. for dedicated/plans we can map unit-based metering (tokens or inference-minutes) to your SKU. we'll coordinate with your billing team.
[06:36] Marco Rivera: do you have recommended default prompts and prompt-engineering suggestions for quantized models?
[06:41] Daniel Ruiz: yes we'll include a prompt appendix and an eval harness. we can also share a small benchmark sheet with token counts, latency, and quality deltas for int8 vs fp16 for the models you plan to use.
[06:56] Sofia Tran: is there an audit trail for admin actions? we need to see who rolled which model and when.
[07:02] Daniel Ruiz: yes audit logs are available per-tenant, and can be shipped to your SIEM; we also support immutable append-only logs for compliance use-cases.
[07:12] Ahmed El-Sayed: excellent. any regulatory or data residency red flags? some customers in EU want data never to leave EU regions.
[07:19] Maya Chen: we can pin deployments to region and enforce egress rules; for Redwood Private we can deploy in your VPC to keep data in-region. we'll include region pinning in the ref-arch.
[07:31] Marco Rivera: how do we validate cost? we need an estimate per 1000 tokens for each site profile.
[07:38] Priya Patel: we'll produce a unit cost calculator: tokens per second estimates, GPU utilization baseline, and cost per minute per model size. that'll be in the runbook so you can plug your cloud rates.
[07:51] Lena Korhonen: ok, on networking for air-gapped installs — what telemetry do you require vs optional?
[07:57] Daniel Ruiz: minimal required: license activation during initial offline registration (signed file exchange), optional: periodic metrics ingestion if allowed. all telemetry can be disabled for fully air-gapped customers.
[08:10] Ahmed El-Sayed: good. for the marketplace listing we'll need a short marketing blurb and a technical spec. can Redwood draft the initial listing copy?
[08:18] Maya Chen: yes we'll draft listing copy and share a doc with suggested screenshots and a 1-page tech spec. would Polaris like to co-author?
[08:25] Marco Rivera: yes co-authoring is ideal — we want to ensure the deploy steps are accurate.
[08:29] Maya Chen: i'll set that as an action item.
[08:33] Daniel Ruiz: one more technical note - monitoring: we provide Prometheus metrics endpoints out of the box and Grafana dashboards; for edge we'll include a minimal dashboard in the helm chart.
[08:43] Sofia Tran: perfect. how about secrets management on the edge — can you integrate with HashiCorp Vault?
[08:49] Priya Patel: yes we support Vault, native cloud KMS and a pluggable secrets provider. we'll document the steps.
[08:56] Ahmed El-Sayed: do you have any preflight checklist for customers? like firewall ports, kernel drivers for GPUs, docker runtime versions.
[09:04] Daniel Ruiz: yes we'll send a preflight checklist; it includes kernel driver versions, nvidia runtime version, containerd or docker compat, and required ports (443 for broker, 9000 for internal metrics by default but configurable).
[09:18] Marco Rivera: Marco again — question on rolling upgrades: can we do canary rollouts across edge fleet?
[09:23] Daniel Ruiz: yes rollout policies supported — canary, percentage-based, and we support immediate rollback to pinned model versions.
[09:32] Lena Korhonen: ok great. quick question about licensing: for offline installs do you support time-limited licenses?
[09:39] Maya Chen: yes we support time-limited entitlements and node counts in the license file.
[09:44] Ahmed El-Sayed: earlier you mentioned fallback to hosted cloud; how are credentials handled for that?
[09:50] Daniel Ruiz: credentials are per-tenant API keys stored encrypted; fallback requires explicit enablement. for fully regulated customers we recommend disabled fallback and a dedicated private deployment.
[09:59] Priya Patel: i'll note that in the ref-arch doc.
[10:02] Maya Chen: ok it looks like we have a set of clear asks. let's recap the main outputs and owners.
[10:09] Daniel Ruiz: runbook + sizing (Daniel) — due 2026-10-18.
[10:14] Priya Patel: ref-arch diagrams + helm skeleton (Priya) — due 2026-10-19.
[10:18] Lena Korhonen: we'll send site inventories and network constraints (Lena) — due 2026-10-16.
[10:23] Sofia Tran: security questionnaire responses (Sofia) — due 2026-10-15.
[10:29] Maya Chen: Redwood will share SOC2 attestation link and draft listing copy by 2026-10-16.
[10:36] Ahmed El-Sayed: Polaris will confirm pilot sites and provide test data by 2026-10-18.
[10:42] Marco Rivera: also want to align on who monitors the KPIs during pilot — we'll assign an ops contact and want daily syncs for the first three days.
[10:50] Maya Chen: sounds good — we'll schedule daily 30m check-ins for smoke + initial perf.
[10:56] Daniel Ruiz: i'll also prepare a perf checklist and a spreadsheet to capture latency, qps, and token cost per run.
[11:03] Maya Chen: final note on co-marketing: once pilot shows green we'll draft a joint solution brief and a marketplace co-listing blurb; legal will need to sign off on logos.
[11:15] Ahmed El-Sayed: ok that works. any other questions?
[11:18] Lena Korhonen: none from me.
[11:20] Marco Rivera: none.
[11:22] Sofia Tran: nope.
[11:23] Maya Chen: great thanks all, i'll follow up with an email with links to the materials and calendar invites for the pilot.
[11:30] Meeting end.
